fixes.correction: The linen bandage must be on De Lannoy's LEFT hand and wrist. He faces the viewer, so his left hand is on the FRAME-RIGHT side of his body, the side where his sheathed sword hangs. Wrap that hand and wrist in clean white linen, and draw his right hand (frame-left side of his body) as bare, unbandaged skin with no wrapping at all. Keep everything else from the previous attempt: bareheaded, pale wavy hair tied back with a black ribbon, the torn, soot-stained blue coat with brass buttons over a dirty white shirt and breeches, sword sheathed, head turned toward the silent line of bare-chested Nair spearmen at frame-right, other Dutch soldiers behind him at frame-left, the burnt stockade and the distant ships, and open sky across the top of the frame for the captions.
fixes.issues: v01: De Lannoy faces the viewer, and the linen bandage is on the wrist of the arm coming from the frame-left side of his body, which is his RIGHT hand. His left hand (frame-right, beside the sword hilt) is bare. The bible and MUST MATCH require the bandage on his LEFT hand and wrist in every panel, and later close-ups (10.1, 11.2) show the bandaged left hand. Everything else works: pale hair with black ribbon, torn soot-stained blue coat, sheathed sword, eyes on the Nair line, open sky for captions.

fixes.correction: Nagoji's ear ornament must be a tiny flush gold stud sitting on the earlobe with nothing hanging below it, not a drop. His RIGHT forearm, the one on the frame-left side of his body holding the reins, must be plain unmarked skin: no brand, no scar, no marks of any kind. Turn his LEFT forearm (frame-right side of his body) so its inner side faces away from the viewer, keeping the brand out of sight. Keep everything else from the previous attempt: Dhanaji frame-left on a dark brown horse (short black beard, white pagdi, indigo quilted tunic, no sash, gesturing as he speaks); Nagoji frame-right on Kayal, a bay mare with a black mane and no white markings (rust-red turban, cream tunic with sleeves rolled to mid-forearm, broad red sash, boots, talwar, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin); the two turbaned riders and a matchlock half hidden in the dune hollow at upper left; the burnt camp and distant ships at right; and clear sky above and between the two heads for Dhanaji's two balloons.
fixes.issues: v01: Nagoji faces the viewer, and the brand and long scar are drawn on the forearm on the frame-left side of his body (the hand on the reins), which is his RIGHT forearm. The brand belongs only on the inner LEFT forearm, and this panel does not call for it to show. His ear ornament is also a small gold drop hanging below the lobe, not the flush stud. Otherwise good: Dhanaji frame-left matches his sheet, Kayal is a bay with no white markings, the hidden riders with a matchlock are in the dune hollow, and there is room for balloons in the sky above the two heads.

fixes.correction: Keep Ramayyan exactly as drawn: bare-headed, thin, receding curly hair, plain white cloth with no border, seated on the same brown horse at frame-left, reins in one hand. Keep the bare-chested Nair spearmen behind him, the charred stockade, the distant ships and the open blue sky in the upper right for the balloons. Change the Dutch. They have just marched out and have NOT surrendered yet, so nobody sits and no musket, hat, sword or other weapon lies on the sand. At the right edge of the frame, show the front rank of the Dutch column STANDING, seen from behind or cut off by the frame edge so that no Dutch face can be read: blue coats, boots and muskets still held upright in their hands, with a clear strip of bare sand in front of their boots. Include no pale-haired man and no officer in a sash. Ramayyan's free hand drops from the elbow, angled DOWNWARD with the open palm toward the ground, pointing at that strip of sand in front of the Dutch boots. It is a small, calm, unhurried gesture, not an arm held out at shoulder height.
fixes.issues: Ramayyan himself is on-model (bare-headed, receding curly hair, plain white cloth, same brown horse as 3.1). The story beat is broken: the three Dutch soldiers sit slumped on the sand with their muskets and a tricorn already lying on the ground. That shows the surrender as already done, which contradicts the line 'Now you will drop the arms', panel 3.2 (Donnadi standing, sword sheathed) and panel 3.4 (Dutch hands tightening on muskets). The seated soldier in the middle has pale curly hair and could be misread as De Lannoy. Ramayyan's arm is held out level at shoulder height, more a point than the small downward palm-down gesture the script asks for.

fixes.correction: Reframe as a tight close-up of hands only. Use a low camera at waist height with the soldiers cropped at the chest, so that NO face, chin or beard appears anywhere in the frame. Across the frame, show a row of four or five Dutch hands in blue coat sleeves with buff turned-back cuffs, clenched hard on the wooden stocks and barrels of upright flintlock muskets. In the centre, show Donnadi's right hand gripping the brass hilt of his sword, which is still SHEATHED in its scabbard at his left hip. The knuckles are pale and strained. Behind the hand are his blue officer's coat with gilt buttons and gold edging and the crimson sash, as in the previous panel. No blade is drawn. Above the hands and musket muzzles, keep the top third of the frame as plain open blue sky over the pale dunes for the two captions.
fixes.issues: The framing is wrong. The script asks for a close insert on hands, but this is a medium group shot with five faces dominating. Donnadi has a full short beard here, while panel 3.2 on the same page gives him a moustache only. His sword is out, a naked blade hanging below the hilt, when it should still be sheathed at his hip (3.2). His knuckles do not read as white with strain. The hands and the setting are otherwise sound.

fixes.correction: Keep everything as drawn: Nagoji on the bay mare Kayal on the dune at frame-left, holding the brass spyglass to his eye with his left hand. Keep the rust-red turban, cream tunic with sleeves pushed up, broad red sash, boots and talwar, and the pale puckered brand and long thin white scar on the inner left forearm. Keep the burnt Dutch camp and distant ships below and the open blue sky in the upper right. Fix only the ear and the jaw. His ear ornament is ONE tiny gold stud sitting flush on the earlobe, a single small dot, with NO bead, ball, ring or drop hanging beneath it. His chin and jaw are smooth and clean-shaven, with no grey shading, stubble or beard texture.
fixes.issues: Almost right. Nagoji is on the bay mare on the dune, holding a brass spyglass, in the rust-red turban, red sash and cream tunic, with a thick curled moustache. His pushed-up left sleeve correctly shows the pale brand and the long white scar on the inner forearm. The burnt camp and ships are below, and the open sky works for the caption. It fails the ear rule: under zoom, the ear ornament is a stud with a second gold bead hanging below it, a drop earring like the sheet's. The bible and the author's decision require a single tiny flush stud with nothing hanging from it. The jaw also has faint grey patchy shading that could read as stubble.

fixes.correction: De Lannoy's costume is wrong. Draw him in the torn, soot-stained Dutch East India Company blue officer's coat with brass buttons, a soiled cream waistcoat and shirt, breeches and black boots, exactly as on page 3 of this chapter. Do NOT use the white tunic-coat, white mundu or sandals from his reference sheet. Use that sheet only for his face, his pale wavy hair tied back with a black ribbon, and his height. Keep everything else that worked. De Lannoy stands a head taller than Donnadi, at his shoulder, and steadily holds Donnadi's gaze, with the linen bandage round his LEFT hand and wrist. Donnadi wears his blue officer's coat with the red waist sash and brass-hilted sword and looks up at him. Keep the slumped, hollow-eyed Dutch soldiers at left, the ring of bare-chested Nair spearmen in white mundus at right, and the open sky at upper left for the balloon.
fixes.issues: De Lannoy is drawn in the white tunic-coat and white mundu from his reference sheet. The chapter 15 bible row (pages 1 to 13.2) and the MUST MATCH line require the torn, soot-stained Dutch blue coat with boots, as on page 3. This breaks continuity with the neighbouring panels. Everything else works: he is a head taller, has pale hair and a bandaged LEFT hand, and holds Donnadi's gaze. The slumped Dutch soldiers are at left, the Nair spear ring is at right, and there is sky for the balloon.

fixes.correction: Donnadi has just unbuckled and dropped his only sword. He must carry NO sword, scabbard, hilt, baldric or sword belt anywhere on his body: no hilt at his hip and no strap across his chest, only his blue coat and sash. In the sand lies the brass-hilted sword, still sheathed in its dark leather scabbard and attached to the unbuckled brown sword belt as one object, as in the previous panel. Its brass guard with an interlaced pattern catches the sun, and sand grains are still settling around it. Frame at sand level so that only Donnadi's black boots and lower legs, cropped at the knee, stand just behind the sword. His face is out of frame, because his line comes from off panel. Keep the column of blue-coated, tricorned Dutch soldiers waiting behind him, the bare-chested Nair spearmen on the dune at right, and the open blue sky at upper left for the caption and balloon.
fixes.issues: Donnadi still wears a sword. A brass hilt and scabbard hang from a baldric at his left hip while 'his' sword and belt lie in the sand, which contradicts the surrender beat. The sword in the sand is also a bare blade lying apart from the belt, whereas panel 4.4 shows it sheathed on the belt. His whole figure and face are in frame, although the script gives only his boots and makes his line come from off panel. The rest works: the sand-level view, the column of tricorned blue coats waiting, the Nair spearmen on the dune, and the open sky at upper left.

fixes.correction: Draw De Lannoy in true profile facing LEFT, so his LEFT side is nearest the viewer, with the white linen bandage wrapped round his LEFT hand and wrist clearly visible on the near hand hanging at his side; his right hand is bare and mostly hidden behind his body. Keep his face, pale wavy hair tied in a queue with a black ribbon, the torn, soot-stained blue coat, open shirt and dirty breeches, and his head tilted up toward the fort. The bowed prisoners around him are his fellow Dutch East India Company soldiers from the same march: European men with sunburnt pale skin and fair, brown or dark hair, bare-headed, in sweat-stained linen shirts with rolled sleeves, dark waistcoats and breeches, a few in torn blue coats, all with heads bowed and hands free, no ropes. No Indian villagers among the prisoners: no turbans, no dhotis, no shoulder cloths on them; at most one bare-chested Nair guard with a topknot, white mundu, small round shield and spear at the edge of the column. Keep the red earth road, the coconut palms and paddy, and the granite walls and round bastions of Udayagiri on the rocky green hill filling the background on the side he looks toward, with a clear patch of open sky in one upper corner for the caption.
fixes.issues: Only candidate v01 fails two ways. (1) De Lannoy's bandage is on the wrong hand: he faces right, three-quarter toward the viewer, and the bandaged hand is the near arm on the image-left side of his body, i.e. his RIGHT hand; the bible requires the linen bandage on his LEFT hand and wrist in every panel. (2) The bowed prisoners around him are drawn as Indian villagers in turbans, dhotis and shoulder cloths, not the Dutch Company soldiers of 5.1 and 5.3, so the beat (the only upright head among his fellow prisoners) reads wrongly. His face, pale wavy hair with black-ribboned queue, torn soot-stained blue coat, upward gaze and the Udayagiri background otherwise work.

fixes.correction: Keep this composition (sea and boats at frame-left, the burned stockade, rope, metal and canvas filling frame-right, open sky above), but fix the side of Ibrahim's scar and his feet. Ibrahim is barefoot, as when he stepped ashore in the previous panel, with no sandals. He faces the viewer and turns his head slightly toward frame-LEFT, looking at Nagoji who stands outside the frame on the left, while his LEFT arm still sweeps out with the open palm toward frame-right across the wreckage, a salesman showing goods without looking at them. This angle shows his LEFT cheek and LEFT ear (on the frame-right side of his face), and that is where the thin pale scar runs, from the left ear down to the jaw. His RIGHT cheek, right ear and the right side of his jaw are smooth and completely unmarked, with no scar, line or scratch.
fixes.issues: Ibrahim's scar is on the wrong side: his body faces us and his head turns to frame-right toward the wreck, which shows his RIGHT cheek and right ear, and the thin pale scar is painted there; the bible and his sheet put it on his LEFT side (page 6 panel 1 has it correctly on the left). He also wears sandals here although he stepped ashore barefoot in the previous panel. Otherwise the gesture, burned stockade and salvage, and sky space for three balloons are good.

fixes.correction: Keep everything in this composition exactly as it is (Ibrahim on the left gesturing at the provisions, Nagoji on the right with his right hand resting on an open rice sack and his left hand on his hip, the crew unloading the second boat, sacks of rice, bundles of dried fish and brass jars of coconut oil in the foreground, open sky top-left). Fix only Nagoji's forearms: his RIGHT forearm, the one reaching down to the rice sack on the frame-left side of his body, is plain smooth skin with NO scar, no white line, no brand and no dark patch of any kind. The pale puckered brand and the single long thin white scar exist only on the inner side of his LEFT forearm, the arm bent with the hand on his hip at frame-right, and there they may show only faintly.
fixes.issues: Nagoji has a long thin white scar and a dark patch on his RIGHT forearm (the arm reaching down to the rice sack), in addition to the brand and scar on his left forearm on his hip; the bible puts the brand and the long white scar only on the inner LEFT forearm, so both arms now read as scarred. Everything else works: crew unloading the second boat, rice sacks, dried fish, oil jars, Nagoji looking down at the sacks, Ibrahim correct (his scarred left side is turned away), wide sky top-left for the balloons.

fixes.correction: Keep this composition exactly (Ibrahim at frame-left facing frame-right, Nagoji at frame-right facing him, the surf and boats behind, the burned stockade at the right edge, open sky in the upper left, Ibrahim unsmiling and tapping his chest with two fingers of his right hand, Nagoji's brand and thin white scar only on the inner side of his LEFT forearm). Fix only Ibrahim's face: because he faces frame-right, his RIGHT cheek, right ear and the right side of his jaw are toward the viewer, and they must be smooth and completely unmarked, with no scar, pale line or scratch. His scar runs from his LEFT ear to the jaw on the far side of his face, turned away from the viewer and not visible in this panel.
fixes.issues: Ibrahim's scar is on the wrong side: he stands at frame-left in profile facing frame-right, so we see his RIGHT cheek and right ear, and the thin pale scar is painted on that right cheek; the bible and his sheet put it from the LEFT ear to the jaw. The rest is good: face-to-face two-shot at the waterline, Ibrahim unsmiling and tapping his chest with two fingers, Nagoji correct with the brand and scar on his inner LEFT forearm, open sky top-left for both balloons.

fixes.correction: Keep the wide strip, the open sky above the boats, the wreckage and palms at frame-left, the crew and boats in the surf at frame-right, and Nagoji in the left foreground seen from behind, his face only in lost profile, his left hand on his hip beside the talwar at his left hip. Fix his arms: seen from behind, his LEFT arm is the one on the frame-left side with the hand on the hip, and his RIGHT arm hangs at the frame-right side of his body. That RIGHT forearm must be plain smooth skin with NO brand, no scar, no white line and no pale patch. The brand and the long thin white scar are only on the inner side of his LEFT forearm, which from behind is turned away from the viewer, so no forearm mark is visible at all in this panel. Also show Ibrahim wading OUT: knee-deep in the surf with his back half-turned to us as he heads toward his boats at the right, looking back over his LEFT shoulder (the shoulder on the frame-left side) toward Nagoji with the merchant's grin and one hand raised in farewell, so his LEFT cheek, with the thin pale scar from the left ear to the jaw, faces the viewer.
fixes.issues: Nagoji, seen from behind, has the brand (a pale lacy patch) and the long white scar painted on his RIGHT forearm, the arm hanging at the frame-right side of his body (his talwar is at his left hip on the frame-left side, so this is his right arm); the bible puts them only on the inner LEFT forearm. Secondary: Ibrahim faces the shore with his arm out as if wading in, rather than wading back out toward his boats and calling over his shoulder. The wide strip, grin, open sky above the boats and Nagoji's face (moustache, stud) are good.

fixes.correction: Nagoji's RIGHT forearm is plain, unmarked skin: no scar, brand, white line, leaf or feather shape of any kind. His only marks are on the INNER LEFT forearm (a small pale puckered patch of raised ridges and a thin white scar toward the elbow). In this panel turn that inner side away from the viewer so that neither forearm shows any mark. No red dot, tilak or any other mark on his forehead. Keep everything else as drawn. Varma, in the cream-and-gold turban with the peacock-feather crest, points south down the coast with his arm stretched toward the sea on the right. Nagoji stands beside him in the rust-red turban, cream tunic with sleeves rolled, and red sash, with a clean-shaven chin. Dhanaji, in a white pagdi, indigo quilted tunic and short black beard, sits in the saddle of his brown horse behind Nagoji. The burnt stockade stands on the beach, and the open sky stays clear in the upper part of the frame.
fixes.issues: Nagoji has a bright white leaf-shaped brand with a long white line on his RIGHT forearm. A similar leaf mark is on his left forearm, so the brand reads as appearing on both arms, in the wrong shape. It contradicts the bible and the correct left-only brand in panel 7.1. He also has a small red dot or tilak at the forehead, and the bible says no forehead marks. The rest works: Varma points south in his crested turban, Dhanaji (white pagdi, indigo quilted tunic, short beard) is in the saddle of his brown horse behind Nagoji, and the beach and sky are clear.

fixes.correction: Kayal has a solid bay face: no star, blaze, snip or any white mark on her forehead or muzzle, and no white anywhere on her body or legs. She has an ochre red-brown coat, black mane and tail, black lower legs, and dark hooves drawn as normal hooves. Every Dutch soldier stays upright or crouched over his musket with his head up. No figure lies, slumps or sits half-submerged in the stream, and nothing reads as a fallen body. Keep the rest of the composition as drawn. Nagoji, in the rust-red turban and red sash, rides Kayal on the left, wheeling left with his talwar raised. Dhanaji, in a white pagdi and indigo quilted tunic, charges through the splashing stream on his brown horse with the Maravar scouts behind him. The Dutch, in blue coats and black tricorns with fixed bayonets, stand behind the palm-log barricades on the right, their volley smoke blowing back into their faces. Leave the open sky at the upper right clear for the two captions.
fixes.issues: Kayal has a clear white star on her forehead, which breaks the rule of no white markings anywhere. Her front hooves are drawn as odd cup-like cylinders. A dark half-submerged figure lies in the stream behind the kneeling musketeer and reads as a fallen body. The staging is otherwise good: Nagoji wheels left with his talwar up, Dhanaji charges through the stream, the Dutch in blue coats and tricorns hold fixed bayonets behind palm-log barricades, the smoke blows back, and the sky at the upper right is open.

fixes.correction: Varma wears NO cross, pendant or religious symbol of any kind. His necklaces are plain gold bead strands only. The small gold St Thomas cross with flared, budded arms appears ONLY on Mathoo Tharakan's chain. Varma's hair is pure jet black, with no grey, gathered in a side knot above his LEFT ear, not a bun on the crown. Nagoji's cream sleeves are down to his wrists, so no brand or scar shows. Ramayyan is clean-shaven, as on his sheet. Keep everything else from the previous attempt: the composition, the granite room with one window onto green hills and drilling spearmen, Nagoji standing by the timber door in his rust-red turban and red sash, Tharakan in dark maroon silk and gold chains and Ramayyan with stylus and palm leaves on the mats, Varma seated on the low platform with the spear leaning beside him, the brass lamp, and the clear upper stone wall for the caption.
fixes.issues: v01 has the right room, window, cast and caption space, but Varma wears a gold Latin cross pendant on his necklaces. That borrows Tharakan's identifying symbol and makes the Hindu king read as Christian, which undercuts the next panel's point that Tharakan is the Syrian Christian at court. Varma's hair is also a bun on the crown, not a side knot above the LEFT ear. Smaller problems: Nagoji's sleeves are rolled up, so the brand shows (on the outer forearm) although the script does not call for it. Ramayyan has a small moustache that is not on his sheet. Tharakan's cross is a plain Latin cross, not the flared, budded St Thomas form.

fixes.correction: This is a CLOSE-UP of Mathoo Tharakan ALONE: his head and chest fill the lower two thirds of the frame, and NO other person appears anywhere (no king, no guard at the door, no bearded courtier, no figures through a window). Behind him is only a plain, softly daylit granite wall, and the upper third of the frame stays clear wall for two captions. Keep his look exactly as in the previous attempt: grey receding curly hair, fine grey moustache, clean chin, a dark maroon silk tunic with gold trim under heavy gold chains. One chain carries a small gold St Thomas (Nasrani) cross with flared, budded ends on each arm, not a plain Latin cross and not a crucifix. He has a calm, assured expression, and his hand may rest at his chest below the cross.
fixes.issues: The script calls for 'Tharakan, close', but v01 is a wide group shot that adds three uncast figures. A bearded bare-chested courtier sits where Ramayyan belongs and does not match him. A brown-clad guard in a maroon turban with a talwar stands at the door, where Nagoji stood in 8.1, and reads as a wrong Nagoji. A Varma-like king sits on the platform with his hair tied back, not in a side knot. Tharakan himself is well drawn, but his cross is a plain Latin cross, not the flared, budded St Thomas form.

fixes.correction: Keep De Lannoy and the two bare-chested Nair spear guards exactly as drawn in the previous attempt: tall, pale hair tied with a black ribbon, the torn, soot-stained blue coat, boots, and a fresh linen bandage on his LEFT hand and wrist, walking in without bowing between the guards in short white mundus. The guards' topknots are tied forward over the forehead. Frame the shot at the timber door and the bare granite wall so that the platform and the seated court are OUT OF FRAME. Draw no other people, no seated figures and no bearded men anywhere, and no third figure at the left edge. Keep the clear upper wall above and beside De Lannoy's head for his balloon, with daylight from the window falling across the floor.
fixes.issues: De Lannoy is right: pale hair tied with a black ribbon, the torn, soot-stained blue coat, boots, the linen bandage on his LEFT hand, and an unbowed stride between two bare-chested spear guards. But the platform at right holds a heavily BEARDED king figure (gold chains, cream and gold mundu, spear behind him) who will read as Varma with a beard. Next to him sit two more bearded men in place of Ramayyan and Tharakan. This contradicts 8.1, 8.4 and 8.5. The guards' topknots sit on the crown, not tied forward as the script says, and a third booted figure stands at the left edge.

fixes.correction: Varma's hair is solid jet black, with NO grey or silver strands at the temples or anywhere, gathered in a side knot above his LEFT ear, not tied at the nape. Keep everything else exactly as in the previous attempt: the view from behind De Lannoy's shoulder (pale hair tied with a black ribbon, the torn, soot-stained blue coat, his bandaged LEFT hand hanging at his side in the foreground), Varma seated on the low stone platform with one forearm resting on his raised knee, looking up at the prisoner without hurry, the spear leaning at left, the brass oil lamp, the window onto green hills with drilling spearmen, and the clear upper granite wall between the window and De Lannoy's head for two balloons.
fixes.issues: Composition, setting and De Lannoy are excellent: the over-the-shoulder view, pale hair with a black ribbon, the torn blue coat, and the bandage on his correct (LEFT) hand. But Varma shows a distinct grey-silver streak at the temple, against the MUST MATCH rule of black hair with never the grey of the later figure. His hair is also tied low at the nape behind the right ear, not in a side knot above the LEFT ear. Both clash with a corrected 8.1 and with the identity lock.

fixes.correction: De Lannoy is still in his torn, soot-stained Dutch BLUE officer's coat over a stained shirt, with dark breeches and boots, exactly as in the previous panels. He does NOT wear a white tunic-coat or a white mundu in this scene. The linen bandage is on his LEFT hand and wrist, the hand farther from Varma, and his right hand is bare. Varma's hair is solid jet black, with no grey strands, in a side knot above his LEFT ear. Keep the composition of the previous attempt: a two-shot in profile across the room, De Lannoy standing at left by the timber door with his mouth open to answer, Varma seated on the low stone platform at right with one hand lifted a little, the spear leaning beside him, the brass lamp, the window onto green hills, and the broad clear granite wall above and between the two heads for three balloons.
fixes.issues: De Lannoy wears the white tunic-coat and white mundu that the bible reserves for page 13 panel 4 onward, not the torn, soot-stained blue coat he wears in 8.3 and 8.4, so the costume jumps between panels on the same page. His bandage is on his RIGHT hand, not his left. Varma again has grey streaks at the temple, against the black-hair rule. Composition, Varma's lifted hand, De Lannoy's open mouth, the room and the clear wall space for three balloons all work.

fixes.correction: Marthanda Varma's hair must be jet black throughout, with no grey or silver strands at the temples, in the side knot or anywhere else. He is a vigorous man in his thirties, matching panel 9.1: bare-headed, black hair in a side knot above his LEFT ear, bare-chested, cream mundu with a gold border, gold necklaces, spear leaning within reach on the platform. Only Tharakan has grey hair. Keep the rest of this composition: Tharakan seated cross-legged on the mat at left in a dark maroon silk tunic with heavy gold chains and the small gold St Thomas cross, gesturing softly with open hands; Varma seated on the low stone platform at right, chin in hand, listening; the window between them onto the yard where bare-chested Nair spearmen drill. Draw only these two men, with no guard by the door. Set any brass oil lamp directly on the floor or the platform, never on a table or box. Keep the top third of the frame as plain granite wall so there is clear space for two balloons.
fixes.issues: Varma's hair is plainly salt-and-pepper, with grey streaks through the hair and the side knot, so he reads older. This breaks the MUST MATCH lock (black hair, never the grey of the sheet's later figure) and does not match the black-haired Varma in 9.1. Smaller problems: an extra bare-chested guard with a red waist sash stands by the door, where Nagoji stands in this room, which muddies the two-shot. The brass lamps stand on a wooden table or box in the bottom-right foreground, and the setting says no tables. Tharakan is good: maroon silk, gold chains, small budded gold cross, grey hair and moustache.

fixes.correction: De Lannoy stands upright in the near foreground at left, seen from behind over his LEFT shoulder as in 8.4, never sitting on the floor. Show his pale wavy hair tied with a black ribbon and his torn, soot-stained blue coat. The linen bandage is on his LEFT hand and wrist only: that hand hangs at his side on the frame's left edge, nearest the camera, and his right hand is bare. Marthanda Varma's hair is jet black with no grey at all, matching 9.1, tied in a side knot above his LEFT ear. Keep the rest: Varma seated on the low stone platform at centre, his spear leaning beside him, eyes fixed on De Lannoy while he tilts his head toward Tharakan. Tharakan sits on the mat at right in dark maroon silk, his heavy gold chains and small gold St Thomas cross catching the window light. Keep the plain granite wall in the upper centre and upper right clear for two balloons.
fixes.issues: Seen from behind, De Lannoy's linen bandage is on his RIGHT wrist (the arm hanging from his right shoulder, on the frame's right side). The lock says the bandage is on the LEFT hand and wrist in every panel. He also sits cross-legged on the floor mat, while 8.4, 8.5 and 10.1 show him standing before the seated Varma. Varma's hair again shows grey streaks at the temples and through the side knot, against the black-hair lock. Tharakan is good, with his gold chains catching the light, and the over-the-shoulder framing and Varma's gaze toward De Lannoy work.

fixes.correction: Varma's hair must be entirely jet black, with no grey, silver or white strands at the temple, above the ear or anywhere else. Draw it gathered into a single compact knot above his LEFT ear, as in the previous panel, with no loose mass of curls hanging down the back of his neck. Keep everything else exactly as it is: the over-the-shoulder view from behind Varma's bare right shoulder with the cream-and-gold cloth and gold bead necklace, his gold drop earring and moustache in profile, the spear at right. Keep De Lannoy standing by the timber door in the torn, soot-stained blue coat, blue breeches and boots, his right hand gripping his own lapel and the linen bandage on his LEFT wrist. Keep the brass lamp, the window with drilling Nair spearmen and green hills, and the plain granite wall between De Lannoy and the window clear for the balloons.
fixes.issues: Varma, seen large over his shoulder, has a clear grey-silver streak at the temple above his right ear. This breaks the MUST MATCH rule (black hair, never the grey of the sheet's later figure) and clashes with his solid black hair in panels 1 and 5. His hair is also a loose mass hanging to the neck below a back-of-head bun, not a compact knot above the left ear. Everything else works: De Lannoy in the torn blue coat and boots, right hand on his lapel, bandaged left wrist, door and brass lamp, window with drilling spearmen, and a plain wall for balloons.

fixes.correction: Make this a TIGHT close-up insert of Ramayyan alone. No other person appears anywhere in the frame: no King on a platform, no man in maroon, no guard or figure at the door, and no window or yard. Frame from just above his bowed, balding head with receding dark curls down to his lap. His head is lowered and turned down at the upper left, eyes on his work, never looking up. His thin, steady fingers hold the metal stylus scoring a single palm leaf resting on the bundle in his lap, lower centre. Show only fine incised lines on the leaf, nothing legible. He wears plain unbordered white cloth draped over one shoulder, with no jewellery, forehead marks or sacred thread. Behind him is only a plain, softly shadowed granite wall. Keep the upper right half of the frame that quiet, empty wall for three speech balloons.
fixes.issues: This is not a tight insert. It is a wide room shot with three extra figures, and Ramayyan should be the only person in the panel. A full-bearded, bare-headed man sits on the King's platform, so he reads as a wrong Varma. A heavy man in maroon sits on the mat, and a bare-chested guard with a spear stands at the door where Nagoji should be. Ramayyan himself is acceptable: thin, receding hair, plain white cloth, head bowed, stylus on a palm-leaf bundle, nothing legible.

fixes.correction: The linen bandage must be on De Lannoy's LEFT hand and wrist only. Because we see him from behind, his left hand is on the LEFT side of the picture: show that left hand bandaged, hanging at his side just clear of the coat skirt. His right hand, on the right side of the picture, rests on the stone sill completely bare, with no bandage or wrapping. The drilling spearmen in the yard below are bare-chested Nair men with forward-tied topknots and white mundus, with no vests or tunics. Keep everything else as it is: De Lannoy half turned from us at the wide window, pale wavy hair tied with a black ribbon, face in profile looking out, the torn, soot-stained blue coat. Keep the timber door and brass lamp at left, the green hills of Travancore under a wide open sky, and the plain floor and low wall along the foot of the panel left quiet for the caption.
fixes.issues: We see De Lannoy from behind: the rear coat pleats and buttons face us. So the bandaged hand on the sill, on the right side of the picture, is his RIGHT hand. The bible requires the bandage on his LEFT hand in every panel, as in panel 2. The drilling spearmen in the yard also wear blue and yellow vests, where panel 1 shows them bare-chested. Otherwise good: half-turned figure at the window, torn blue coat, pale hair with a black ribbon, open sky over green hills, and a quiet floor and wall band at the foot for the caption.

fixes.correction: Below the coat, De Lannoy wears his officer's blue breeches tucked into tall black boots, exactly as in the previous panels. Draw no white skirt, wrap, mundu or sash at his waist. His white waistcoat and shirt show only at the chest under the open coat. Keep all staining to grey-black soot smudges and ash on the blue cloth, with no brown or reddish drips or spatter anywhere. Keep everything else as it is: Nagoji seen from behind in the near foreground at the timber doorframe, with rust-red turban, long curly black hair, tiny gold stud, cream tunic and red sash. Keep De Lannoy standing full-on in the torn blue coat, pale wavy hair, looking straight at Nagoji, linen bandage on his LEFT hand and wrist. Keep Varma small and seated on the platform behind him by the window, bare-headed with his knot, gold necklaces and spear, and the plain granite wall above De Lannoy's head clear for the balloons.
fixes.issues: De Lannoy wears a long white wrap skirt with a white sash under the open blue coat, with no breeches or boots. This mixes in his later white mundu costume, which the bible starts only at page 13 panel 4, and breaks continuity with panel 2 (blue breeches and boots). The white cloth also carries brown drip-and-spatter stains that read as dried blood. Otherwise good: Nagoji over-the-shoulder at the doorframe (rust-red turban, curly black hair, small gold stud, red sash, clean jaw), De Lannoy facing us with his bandaged LEFT hand, and Varma small and seated by the window with his spear.

fixes.correction: Keep this composition: an over-the-shoulder view from behind De Lannoy in the left foreground (pale wavy hair tied with a black ribbon, the torn soot-stained blue coat), and Nagoji standing in the open timber doorway at right with one hand on the doorframe. He wears the commander look: rust-red turban, cream tunic, broad red sash, cream trousers, boots and talwar. Keep the single window with Nair spearmen drilling in the yard at upper left and the plain granite wall in the upper middle, clear for two balloons. Fix three things. First, Nagoji's ear ornament is a single tiny flush gold stud pressed on the lobe, with no bead, ball or drop hanging below it on either ear. Second, his chin and jaw are smooth and clean-shaven, with no stubble, hatching or dark shading under the lower lip or along the jaw; only the thick curled moustache. Third, De Lannoy's linen bandage is on his LEFT hand and wrist only. Seen from behind, his left arm is the one on the LEFT side of his figure in the frame. His right arm, on the right side of the frame nearer Nagoji, ends in a bare hand below the coat cuff, with no wrapping. Paint the coat as plain woven blue wool with torn edges and soot smudges, not a checkered or quilted pattern.
fixes.issues: v01 (the only candidate) fails three character rules. (1) Nagoji's ear ornaments are studs with a gold bead hanging below the lobe on both ears. That is the sheet's drop earring, which the author ruled on 2026-10-02 must be refused at selection. (2) Stubble shading darkens his chin under the lower lip and along the jaw. The commander look requires a smooth, clean-shaven chin. (3) We see De Lannoy from behind, so his right arm is on the right of the frame, and the linen bandage is on that RIGHT wrist. The bible row says LEFT hand and wrist. Minor: the blue coat has a pixelated, checkered quilt texture. What works: the over-the-shoulder reverse angle, Nagoji in the timber doorway with his hand on the doorframe in the full commander look, the window with drilling Nair spearmen, and the clear stone wall in the upper middle for both balloons.

fixes.correction: Keep this tight composition. De Lannoy fills the left and centre in the torn soot-stained blue coat over a stained white shirt, his face high in the frame looking down at his own hands, and both open hands are held out in the foreground. Varma sits soft and out of focus on the low stone platform at right: bare-headed, black hair in a side knot, gold necklaces, spear leaning behind him. Keep the window with drilling Nair spearmen between them, and leave the plain granite wall at the upper left and upper right clear for two balloons and a caption. Fix the hands. Both hands are turned PALMS UP, so we see the palms and finger pads, never the nails or knuckles, and each hand has exactly one thumb and four fingers. The clean plain cream linen bandage, with no brown, rust, red or pink stains, wraps his LEFT hand and wrist. Because he faces us, that is the hand on the RIGHT side of the frame. His right hand, on the left side of the frame, is bare and unwrapped.
fixes.issues: v01 (the only candidate) has three faults. (1) Anatomy: the bare hand on the right of the frame has a thumb plus five fingers with nails, which makes six digits. (2) Handedness: De Lannoy faces us, so the bandaged hand on the left of the frame is his RIGHT. The bible requires the bandage on his LEFT hand and wrist. (3) The bandaged hand shows its back, with nails and knuckles, so it is not palm-up as the script asks. Its wrap is also streaked with rust-brown stains that could read as old blood. What works: the tight framing, his face above the hands looking down, Varma soft and out of focus on the platform beyond (bare-headed, black hair, gold necklaces, spear), the window with drilling spearmen, and wall space at the upper left and upper right.

fixes.correction: Keep this two-shot unchanged in layout. De Lannoy kneels on the woven mat at frame-left in profile facing right, head lifted toward the King, in the torn soot-stained blue coat over a stained white shirt with pale trousers. Varma sits on the low stone platform at frame-right with a faint smile, bare-chested in the gold-bordered cream mundu and gold necklaces, spear leaning behind him. Keep the single window of drilling Nair spearmen between them and the open-wick brass lamps, and leave the plain upper wall clear for the balloons. Fix two things. First, Varma's hair is solid glossy black throughout, tied in a side knot above his LEFT ear, with no grey, silver or white strands at the temples or anywhere else. Second, De Lannoy's bandage is on his LEFT hand and wrist. In this right-facing profile, his left hand is the far hand. Show it resting on his far knee, visible just in front of his body and wrapped in clean plain linen. His near right hand, resting on the near knee, is bare with no wrapping.
fixes.issues: v01 (the only candidate) breaks the Varma MUST MATCH rule: his hair is clearly salt-and-pepper, with silver-grey strands from the temples to the knot. The bible requires black hair, never the grey of the sheet's later figure. De Lannoy is in right-facing profile, and the only visible bandaged arm is his near arm, which is his RIGHT. The bible puts the bandage on his LEFT hand and wrist. What works: the two-shot framing, with De Lannoy kneeling at left, head lifted to the King, and Varma seated at right with a smile on the gold-bordered mundu and spear. The window of drilling spearmen, the open-wick lamps and the clear upper wall and sky also work.

fixes.correction: Keep this wide composition. De Lannoy stands at left beside the open timber door. Ramayyan sits cross-legged on the woven mat at centre in plain white cloth, his stylus moving on a palm-leaf bundle. Varma sits on the low stone platform at right, bare-chested in the gold-bordered cream mundu with gold necklaces, black hair in a side knot, spear leaning behind him, beside an open-wick brass lamp. Keep the single window of drilling Nair spearmen and the plain upper wall clear for two balloons. Fix De Lannoy. He wears the torn soot-stained blue coat over the stained white shirt, with pale breeches tucked into tall brown leather boots. He wears no mundu, no ankle-length white cloth and no sandals. His head dips forward in a slow nod, eyes lowered. The clean linen bandage is on his LEFT hand and wrist. As he stands three-quarter toward Varma, that is the hand hanging at his side on the RIGHT of his figure in the frame. His right hand, on the left of his figure, is bare. Varma's head turns slightly toward Ramayyan in a small nod.
fixes.issues: v01 (the only candidate) dresses De Lannoy wrongly for this page. Under the blue coat he wears an ankle-length white mundu and sandals, the costume reserved for page 13 panel 4 onward. The bible requires the torn blue coat with boots through page 13 panel 2, and panels 3 and 5 of this page show trousers and boots. He stands three-quarter toward Varma, so the bandaged forearm across his chest is his RIGHT arm, while the bible puts the bandage on the LEFT. He also stares sideways rather than giving the slow nod. What works: the wide room with the open door at left, Ramayyan seated cross-legged at centre writing with the stylus on a palm-leaf bundle, and Varma bare-headed with black hair on the platform with his spear. The window with drilling spearmen and the large clear upper wall for both balloons also work.

fixes.correction: Keep this composition unchanged. The open doorway is at left, with De Lannoy seen from behind in the torn soot-stained blue coat, the linen bandage on his LEFT wrist, flanked by two bare-chested Nair spearmen escorting him out. Nagoji stands aside against the wall at centre in the commander look: rust-red turban, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, tiny flush gold ear stud, cream tunic, red sash, talwar and boots. Ramayyan sits on the mat in plain white, looking up from his palm-leaf bundle, and Varma sits on the platform at right watching the door. Keep the window of drilling spearmen, and leave the plain granite wall above Ramayyan and the upper centre clear for two balloons. Fix three things. First, Nagoji's cream tunic sleeves come all the way down to his wrists on both arms, so no forearm skin, brand or scar shows anywhere. Second, Varma's hair is solid glossy black in a side knot, with no grey, silver or white strands. Third, below De Lannoy's coat hem, pale breeches are tucked into his tall brown boots, with no ankle-length white cloth or mundu.
fixes.issues: v01 (the only candidate) shows Nagoji with his sleeves rolled to the elbow. The pale puckered brand and the long white scar sit plainly on his RIGHT forearm: he faces us, with the talwar on his left hip, so the brand is on the arm at the left of the frame. The bible puts the brand on the inner LEFT forearm and shows it only when the panel says his sleeves are pushed up, which this panel does not. Varma's hair carries visible grey streaks at the temple, against the black-hair rule. Under De Lannoy's coat, an ankle-length white cloth reads as a mundu, though his boots are correct. What works: De Lannoy's back in the doorway with the bandage correctly on his LEFT wrist, and the two bare-chested Nair spearmen escorting him. Nagoji stands aside with a clean chin, curled moustache and a flush gold stud. Ramayyan looks up from his leaf, and Varma watches the door. The wall above Ramayyan and the sky in the door and window leave room for two balloons.

fixes.correction: Stage this as a new moment, not a repeat of the previous panel. Marthanda Varma is visibly getting up, half-risen off the low stone platform with his weight coming onto his feet and his knees straightening, and his right hand closes around the shaft of his spear where it leaned against the wall. Nagoji has crossed from the door and now stands just beside and slightly behind Varma's shoulder, within arm's reach, so the two read as a close two-shot. Keep the same private audience room as the previous panel: bare granite walls, woven mats on the low platform, brass oil lamps with open wicks, and the single window with plain wooden uprights. Through the window are green hills and a yard of drilling bare-chested Nair spearmen in white mundus. Varma's hair is black and gathered in one knot above his LEFT ear, not a loose mane. Keep Nagoji exactly as now: rust-red turban, red sash, rolled sleeves showing the pale ridged brand and the thin white scar on his left forearm, boots, talwar, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin and a tiny gold stud. Keep the upper grey wall above both heads clear for two balloons.
fixes.issues: The beat is missed. Varma is still seated on the platform, gripping the spear, and is not rising. Nagoji is still by the far door, not at Varma's shoulder. The composition nearly repeats 12.1. The room does not match 12.1 either: the window has no wooden uprights and shows palm trees. Varma's hair is a loose curly mane with only a vague crown knot, not a clear side knot above the left ear. Everything else works: Nagoji is on model, his brand is a good pale ridged patch beside a white scar, the hands are sound, and the wall is clear for balloons.

fixes.correction: Marthanda Varma's hair must be entirely jet black, with no grey or silver streak at the temple or anywhere else. He is the young king here, not the grey-haired later figure on his sheet. Gather his hair in a single plain knot above his LEFT ear, with no coloured band. Tie the Nair guards' topknots forward at the front of the head. Keep everything else as drawn. Nagoji and Varma walk along the raised upper walk at the left. The Dutch prisoners in stained blue coats and shirtsleeves sit in rows eating rice from leaves and looking up. Bare-chested Nair guards with spears stand at the edges. Keep the hard noon light, the tiled roofs and the green hills. Keep the open band of sky across the top and the plain stone wall behind the prisoners clear for two captions.
fixes.issues: Varma has a prominent grey streak at his temple. The bible says he must never have the grey hair of the sheet's later figure. His knot sits on top of his head and is tied with an orange band, not placed above the left ear. Minor: the Nair guards' topknots are at the back of the head, not forward-tied. Everything else works well. Nagoji and Varma pass along the upper walk. The Dutch prisoners in stained blue coats and shirtsleeves sit eating rice from leaves and look up. The light is high noon, with sky and a plain wall left free for the captions.

fixes.correction: This is a tight close-up on De Lannoy's coat front and hands, and he is the same man as in the previous panel. He is young and clean-shaven, with pale-blond wavy hair tied back in a queue with a black ribbon, as on his sheet; he is not a rugged older man with loose straight hair. His lowered face may appear at the top edge of the frame. The linen bandage is on his LEFT hand and wrist only, and his RIGHT hand is bare. With his body facing the viewer, the bandaged left hand rests low on the viewer's RIGHT side of the picture. The bare right hand comes in from the viewer's LEFT, and its THUMB runs down the row of plain brass coat buttons, each with a worn interlaced mark and no letters. Keep the torn, soot-stained blue coat and the pre-dawn blue-grey courtyard light. Leave clear sky or plain wall in the upper part of the frame for one long balloon.
fixes.issues: The bandage is on the wrong hand. De Lannoy's body is turned so the near, viewer's-left arm is his RIGHT, and that is the arm wrapped in linen; the bare hand touching a button is his LEFT. This breaks the 'bandage on LEFT hand in every panel' rule and the script's 'right thumb'. A fingertip presses a button rather than the thumb running along the row. The face and hair do not match the sheet or 12.4: he is a rugged older man with loose straight golden hair and no ribboned queue. The framing is a mid-shot, not a tight one. The buttons are plain brass with no letters, which is fine, and the pre-dawn courtyard and sky are good for the balloon.

fixes.correction: Keep this composition, the blue pre-dawn light, the oil lamps, the green hills over the wall and Nagoji's outstretched left arm gesturing toward them. Fix De Lannoy's bandage. The linen bandage is on his own LEFT hand and wrist. As he stands facing the viewer, turned three-quarter toward picture-right, his left hand is the one on the picture-RIGHT side of his body, hanging nearest Nagoji, so the bandage goes on that hand. His own right hand, on the picture-left side, is bare with no wrapping. Draw Nagoji's brand as a small pale, shiny, puckered patch of raised scar ridges like an old burn, never an ornamental rosette, medallion or tattoo-like pattern. Put it beside one long thin white scar, and put both only on the inner side of the outstretched LEFT forearm. His right forearm, hanging at his side, is plain unmarked skin.
fixes.issues: v01 (the only candidate) gets the beat, setting and pre-dawn blue light right, and Nagoji's face is on model. De Lannoy's linen bandage is on the wrong hand: the bandaged hand comes out of the picture-left sleeve, so it is his anatomical RIGHT hand. The bible row and MUST MATCH lock it to his LEFT hand, and the neighbouring panels 12.4, 12.5 and 13.2 all show it on the left. Nagoji's brand is drawn as an ornamental, tattoo-like rosette, not a puckered burn scar, and a second white scar line also shows on his right forearm.

fixes.correction: The garment folded on the stone bench in the foreground must be his torn, soot-stained DARK BLUE Dutch officer's coat with plain brass buttons, folded neatly and carefully like a shroud. His brown boots are set side by side beside it, and there is no white garment anywhere on the bench. De Lannoy is not yet wearing the mundu. He stands behind the bench, barefoot, in his sweat-stained shirt open at the throat over pale skin, still in the breeches he wore under the coat. He holds the unworn white mundu up and spread open between both hands at chest height, studying it in puzzlement as if it were a map of an unknown country. The linen bandage is on his own LEFT hand and wrist. As he faces the viewer, that is the hand on the picture-RIGHT side of his body; his right hand, picture-left, is bare. The light is first light: low early sun warming only the tops of the walls, the courtyard floor still in cool blue shadow, with no high midday sun. Keep the courtyard of officers' doorways under tiled roofs, the bench in the right foreground and the open sky at upper left for the balloon.
fixes.issues: v01 (the only candidate) misses the key prop. The garment folded on the bench is WHITE with buttons and reads as the new tunic-coat, so the blue coat is missing from the scene. De Lannoy is already wrapped in the mundu rather than holding it up 'as if it were a map', which also undercuts the 13.4 dressing beat. The bandage is again on his anatomical RIGHT hand, the picture-left one as he faces us. The scene is lit by high midday sun rather than first light.

fixes.correction: Keep this layout: the bordered inset at upper left; De Lannoy at centre in the plain white tunic-coat, white ankle-length mundu and sandals, bare-headed; Nagoji at right in rust-red turban, red sash, cream tunic and boots, stepping back; the blue coat on the bench at left, now neatly folded rather than crumpled; and open sky above for the balloons. Fix the handedness. De Lannoy's linen bandage is on his own LEFT hand and wrist in both the inset and the main image. As he faces the viewer, that is the hand on the picture-RIGHT side of his body; his right hand, picture-left, is bare. Nagoji's brand and his long thin white scar are on his own LEFT inner forearm only. In the main image he faces picture-left toward De Lannoy, so his left arm is the one on the picture-RIGHT side of his body. His right forearm, on the picture-left side and hanging at his side, has the sleeve pushed up over plain unmarked skin. In the inset only one of Nagoji's forearms carries the mark, turned so its INNER palm-side faces the viewer, never the back of the forearm, and the loose end of the white cloth visibly slips from De Lannoy's fingers. The brand is a small pale, puckered patch of raised scar ridges like an old burn, never an ornamental rosette, medallion or tattoo-like design.
fixes.issues: v01 (the only candidate) has a good layout: the upper-left inset, De Lannoy in the white tunic-coat, mundu and sandals, Nagoji stepping back, the blue coat on the bench, and sky for the balloons. The handedness is wrong in three places. (1) De Lannoy's bandage is on his anatomical RIGHT hand, picture-left as he faces us, in both the inset and the main image. (2) In the main image Nagoji's brand and scar are on his RIGHT forearm, the picture-left arm hanging at his side. (3) In the inset the brand sits on the back (outer) side of a palm-down forearm, both of Nagoji's forearms carry scars, and the brand is an ornamental rosette rather than a puckered burn. Also, the blue coat is crumpled, not folded, and the inset does not show the cloth end slipping from De Lannoy's fingers.

fixes.correction: Keep this composition: De Lannoy at picture-left in the plain white tunic-coat and white mundu, pale hair tied with a black ribbon; Nagoji beside him on the raised walk, serious, pointing with his branded left arm down to the Nair squad and their red-sashed captain in the sunlit lower yard; the parapet, the far wall and gate, and the open sky and hills at upper right for the balloons. Fix De Lannoy's bandage. The linen bandage is on his own LEFT hand and wrist. Standing three-quarter toward picture-right, his left arm is the far arm on the picture-RIGHT side of his body, hanging beside Nagoji, so the bandage goes on that hand. His near right arm, coming from the picture-left shoulder, and his right hand are bare with no wrapping. Tie the Nairs' topknots forward, at the front of the crown.
fixes.issues: v01 (the only candidate) shows the beat well: Nagoji on model and serious, pointing with his branded left arm (the brand drawn correctly as a puckered burn) from the raised walk down to a bare-chested Nair squad with spears and a captain in the lower yard, with ample sky for the balloons. The bandage is again on De Lannoy's anatomical RIGHT hand: his near arm, which comes from the picture-left shoulder, as he stands three-quarter toward picture-right. This breaks the LEFT-hand lock. Minor: the shot is side-by-side rather than over De Lannoy's shoulder, and the Nairs' topknots sit on top of the head rather than tied forward.
